(Medievalists.net grounds the inn room programme — hall/chambers/kitchen — but not the vertical placement.)<br>`example_for_TYPE_only`: The New Inn, Gloucester (timber-framed galleried courtyard inn, c.1430-50, ~40 chambers; Wikipedia) attests medieval inns as multi-storey galleried buildings with many guest chambers — evidence for the TYPE + the upstairs-lodging direction, NOT for this 4-bay scale (it is a large 7-bay courtyard inn).<br>`windows.count`: STYLIZED by analogy to the hall-house family — no inn-specific window survey (would need Pantin, Medieval Inns, 1961); per_bay 1.0 on the street front (urban shopfront tier more fenestrated than the rural humble tier is a REASONED, unattested step).
